articles.title: India plans to make its own 350 kmph speed bullet trains by 2030 to match Japan's E10, first B28 trains to run at 249 kmph from 2027; Mumbai-Ahmedabad project cost tops Rs 2 lakh crore
articles.summary: India Business News: Even as it builds the country’s first high-speed train set for the first time, Indian Railways has already set the ball rolling for another set of bul.
articles.body: Even as it builds the country’s first high-speed train set for the first time, Indian Railways has already set the ball rolling for another set of bullet trains that will run at 350 kmph.India is planning to develop and manufacture its own high-speed, or bullet, trains with a design speed of 350 kmph, known as B35, by 2030, according to this TOI report.This would put the indigenous trains on par with Japan's next-generation E10 series, which is also scheduled to enter production in the same year, the report said.The entire 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail corridor is scheduled to be completed by December 2030. But to begin with a small stretch will likely be thrown open in 2027 for which BEML is manufacturing the high-speed train sets that will have a design speed of 280 kmph.Also Read | How Vande Bharat Express marked a tech leap for railways after Rajdhani & Shatabdi. Next stop: Bullet trainsThe Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor will initially run B28 trains Their maximum operating speed, however, will be "249 kmph". BEML has already secured contracts to manufacture 32 B28 trains.Two prototype B28 trains are expected to be ready for trial runs in the first quarter of 2027. BEML said in a filing with the BSE on Friday that it had also received a separate contract worth Rs 5,400 crore for manufacturing another 15 B28 trains.India’s 350 kmph bullet train dreamThe details are part of the railway ministry's Cabinet proposal seeking approval for the revised cost of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) project.The Cabinet has approved a revised project cost of more than Rs 2 lakh crore, almost twice the estimate prepared in 2015. Of the nearly Rs 1 lakh crore increase in the project cost, the additional expenditure will be met through budgetary support.TOI has learnt that the railway ministry told the Cabinet it had begun work on developing B35 trains after Japan communicated in December 2024 that production of its existing E5 series trains was being phased out. Japan indicated that manufacturing of the E10 series would start in 2030, with the trains expected to be ready for operations by 2034.Officials said the possibility of deploying E10 trains would be examined once they become available.The ministry has also said that work on indigenous B28 high-speed trains has already been taken up. Alongside this, India will develop its own Bharat Train Control System (BTCS).The proposed system follows the approach adopted by China with its indigenous CTCS signalling and train control system, which is used to manage train speeds, spacing and safety across both conventional and high-speed railway networks.According to the ministry, the project cost has risen sharply from the earlier estimate of Rs 1.1 lakh crore. A major part of the increase has come from land acquisition, whose cost has more than tripled to around Rs 19,700 crore.Infrastructure expenditure has climbed by nearly 50% to more than Rs 1 lakh crore, while spending on trains and signalling systems has increased by around 100% compared with the estimate made in 2015.Excluding the cost of future Japanese trains, the project now works out to approximately Rs 399 crore per km.B28 bullet train projectThe bullet trains will feature fully air-conditioned chair-car coaches along with world-class passenger facilities. They will also be equipped with advanced onboard infotainment systems, reclining and rotatable seats and dedicated facilities for divyangjans.BEML has set up a dedicated ‘Aditya’ High-Speed Rail Complex in Bengaluru for manufacturing the bullet trains.These high-speed trains will be manufactured using advanced, precision-driven technologies. Bullet trains operating in countries such as Japan and those in Europe are generally designed to function in cold-weather conditions. For the Indian trains, however, the design and manufacturing process will factor in the country's heat and dust conditions.Experts have described the project as a significant engineering step for India. Manufacturing a high-speed bullet train requires a substantially different set of capabilities from those needed to produce the LHB coaches that Indian Railways currently manufactures.In simple terms, developing a bullet train involves much more than making a train capable of travelling at higher speeds. It must be engineered to remain stable and deliver a smooth ride at those speeds.The body needs to combine strength with low weight, while the wheels and suspension systems have to support a stable and comfortable journey. Train control technology also needs to be significantly more advanced to ensure safe operation and maintain passenger comfort during sudden changes in air pressure.The Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train is one among several high-speed rail projects being planned by Indian Railways. The Budget this year announced seven additional high-speed rail corridors. Building domestic bullet train manufacturing capabilities could help meet the rolling stock requirements of these corridors in a cost-effective manner.The proposed routes are Mumbai-Pune, with a travel time of 48 minutes; Pune-Hyderabad, 1 hour 55 minutes; Hyderabad-Bengaluru, 2 hours; Hyderabad-Chennai, 2 hours 55 minutes; Chennai-Bengaluru, 1 hour 13 minutes; Delhi-Varanasi, 3 hours 50 minutes; and Varanasi-Siliguri via Patna, 2 hours 55 minutes.(With inputs from Dipak K Dash)Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Trump traded more securities than all Congress; backs stock-buying ban for all Congress lawmakers, but not president
articles.summary: International Business News: Did you know that US President Donald Trump has carried out more securities trades than all members of Congress combined since his return to the White.
articles.body: Did you know that US President Donald Trump has carried out more securities trades than all members of Congress combined since his return to the White House in January 2025? Interestingly, he supports legislation that would prohibit lawmakers from buying and selling stocks without imposing the same restriction on the president.A majority of Americans support prohibiting lawmakers from trading stocks. President Donald Trump himself backed a ban that would restrict members of Congress but leave him outside its scope.A Bloomberg review of financial disclosures found that Trump or his money managers made nearly 28,700 trades during the 17 months from his second inauguration through the end of June, 2026. In comparison, lawmakers on Capitol Hill reported roughly 22,200 transactions over the same period.The sharp increase in presidential trading has renewed concerns about possible conflicts of interest. The debate has largely focused on whether elected officials could use non-public information when trading, but Kedric Payne of the Campaign Legal Center said that is not the only concern.“Even if they’re not trading the stock on non-public information, they still create the appearance of a conflict of interest because they can still influence the value of the stock through their official duties,” he said.Republicans' stanceRepublicans are also seeking to turn opposition to congressional stock trading into a campaign issue ahead of this fall's closely watched midterm elections.“The American people deserve to know that those they elect to public office actually serve the American people and not their own wallets,” Representative Anna Paulina Luna said during a speech at a two-day Republican convention in Dallas last week.The stock-trading prohibition approved by House Republicans in July applies only to members of Congress, their spouses and dependent children. The president is not covered by the measure. This leaves Trump able to continue trading securities despite having access to a broad range of US intelligence and the ability to affect entire sectors through executive orders or statements on social media.Trump has endorsed the House legislation. In his State of the Union address earlier this year, he urged Congress to approve the measure “without delay” so that lawmakers “cannot corruptly profit from using insider information.”Restrictions on stock trading by lawmakers have attracted support across the political spectrum. An Economist/YouGov poll conducted in May found that three-quarters of US citizens believed members of Congress and other elected officials should not be permitted to trade stocks. A slightly smaller share supported a complete ban.Trump’s investmentsThe White House did not comment on whether Trump supports extending a stock-trading ban to the president. White House spokesman Davis Ingle, however, said Trump's investments are managed independently by third-party financial institutions through computer-based model portfolios that track indexes such as the Schwab 1000.“Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence, or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold,” he said.Trump has previously criticised lawmakers who have sought to extend restrictions on stock trading to the presidency. Last year, after Senator Josh Hawley introduced legislation that would have applied a congressional stock-trading ban to the president and vice president, Trump attacked the Republican senator.The Missouri senator was a “pawn” who was “playing right into the dirty hands of the Democrats,” Trump said on the social media platform he owns.“I don’t think real Republicans want to see their President, who has had unprecedented success, TARGETED, because of the ‘whims’ of a second-tier Senator named Josh Hawley!” Trump said.Trump’s standTrump has also called for an investigation into stock trading involving former House speaker Nancy Pelosi and her husband, whose technology-heavy portfolio has frequently outperformed the broader market. The family's investment choices have become the basis for trading apps and an exchange-traded fund, while also inspiring Hawley's legislation, which was initially titled the Preventing Elected Leaders from Owning Securities and Investments Act, or PELOSI Act.Trump is the only US president this century to have disclosed active trading in individual stocks, averaging about 80 trades on each market day. His financial disclosures during his first term were dominated by relatively illiquid real estate assets and other privately held businesses. His portfolio now includes thousands of positions across stocks, bonds and cryptocurrencies.During the first quarter of this year, Trump purchased as much as $1.38 million worth of shares in DoorDash Inc.In April, the food delivery company delivered a McDonald’s order to Trump at the White House. The event became a social-media moment that promoted tax breaks for tipped workers while also providing a lobbying coup for DoorDash. CNN reported that Trump has also promoted companies including Nvidia Corp., Tesla Inc. and 19 other firms within a week of acquiring stakes in them.‘Everybody’s profiting’Trump has rejected the suggestion that his trading creates a conflict of interest. “You know ⁠why I’m profiting?” he told reporters in July. “Because the stock market’s going up. Everybody’s profiting.”Even a stock-trading prohibition covering members of Congress appears to face significant hurdles. The House measure approved in July was attached to legislation on voter identification that was regarded as a poison pill by Senate Democrats.Hawley was the only Republican on the committee to support his own bill. Other Republicans described the proposal as a “publicity show” and “legislative demagoguery.”The most significant overhaul of congressional financial ethics rules in recent years came with the Stop Trading on Congressional Knowledge Act of 2012, commonly known as the STOCK Act. However, enforcement has remained limited, with penalties beginning at only $200.Applying a stock-trading ban to the president could prove even harder.“The way we’ve handled this in the past is through ethics norms, ethics traditions, public and political pressure,” Payne said. While ethics committees or the Department of Justice could enforce a ban applicable to Congress, “it’s questionable how the DOJ would be able to effectively enforce it against the president.”Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: AMD Set to Top $1 Trillion in Market Value as Chip Stocks Soar
articles.summary: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. shares jumped Monday, putting the company on track to close above $1 trillion in market value for the first time amid renewed opt...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Advanced Micro Devices Inc. shares jumped Monday, putting the company on track to close above $1 trillion in market value for the first time amid renewed optimism for chipmakers necessary to power artificial intelligence.

The stock gained as much as 10% to hit a record high and is on course to join fellow chipmakers Micron Technology Inc, Broadcom Inc., Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd. and Nvidia Corp, with valuations of $1 trillion or more. There are 15 other publicly traded companies in the world worth at least that much, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

Shares of other semiconductor firms also climbed on Monday, as Intel Corp. rose as much as 12% and Arm Holdings Plc gained as much as 14%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index climbed more than 4%, set for its fifth straight session of gains.

At least some of the optimism for chip stocks comes after Meta Platform Inc.'s Muse AI Agent reached the top slot among Apple Inc.'s App Store free applications following its launch earlier this month. That's stoked a renewed frenzy for shares of companies that produce central-processing units, or CPUs, necessary to power agentic AI. Meta shares soared more than 7% on Monday.

"As AI agents gain broader consumer adoption, demand for server CPUs should benefit from higher inference, orchestration, and infrastructure workloads," Jefferies analyst Jacky He wrote in a note.

AMD shares have seen renewed enthusiasm from investors in recent weeks after a two-month period of losses. The stock has gained about 30% so far in September, putting it on track for its best monthly gain since May, after shedding nearly 26% from its June peak to its July trough. Meta is AMD's second-biggest customer, accounting for about 5.5% of its revenue, data compiled by Bloomberg show.

articles.title: How to start buying crypto with $100
articles.summary: Curious about crypto but not ready to risk big money? Learn how to start investing with just $100.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

You don't need thousands of dollars to buy crypto. Many platforms let you buy fractional amounts, so $100 is enough to open a position, learn how the market works, then decide whether crypto belongs in your portfolio.

Just get your mindset right first. Starting with $100 is best viewed as a low-stakes way to gain experience — not a fast track to wealth.

Crypto can be exciting and chaotic. Prices can swing dramatically in a matter of hours, and bad decisions get punished quickly. It isn't for everyone.

But starting with $100 can work in your favor. It gives you room to learn the ropes without putting too much on the line.

Before you buy anything, though, make sure your financial bases are covered. If losing most of that $100 would genuinely muddy your finances, you shouldn't be using it to buy crypto.

Experts generally recommend building an emergency fund and paying off high-interest debt before investing.

Starting with $100 allows you to buy exposure and experience. You're learning how to execute a trade and monitor a position — and maybe most importantly — learning how you react emotionally when your investment jumps or drops.

That mindset matters because people who go in expecting moonshot gains overnight are often the same people who tend to panic sell after the first ugly drop.

"Having unreasonable expectations will usually lead to disappointing results," said Adam Blumberg, a CFP and managing partner at Protocol Wealth in Denver.

Finally, be honest about your risk tolerance. Crypto is a market where drop, exchange failures, hacks, and liquidity problems are all part of the deal. Again, it's not for everyone.

Still on board? Here's how to get started.

Step 1: Educate yourself and get clear on your goals

You don't need to become a technical expert to buy crypto. But it's beneficial to know the basics.

Start by learning a few key concepts: what cryptocurrency is , how buying and selling works , what a wallet is , and why crypto is generally riskier than traditional investments, such as stocks or mutual funds.

Before starting out, it's also wise to get clear on why you're buying crypto in the first place.

"Why you're investing will often drive your expectations and your behaviors," said Blumberg.

Is this $100 just an experiment? Are you planning to add small amounts over time? Do you want to hold long term, or are you trying to actively trade?

Blumberg noted other reasons people may invest in crypto, including wanting a certain uncorrelated return, a hedge against traditional finance, or because they believe in the value of a particular project.

"These various reasons will help you make rational decisions, such as exiting your position when you've reached your goal, or when market or economic conditions change," said Blumberg.

The number of places you can buy cryptocurrency has exploded in recent years. From dedicated exchanges to popular payment apps, you've got options.

Here's an overview of the primary ways you can buy crypto:

Centralized exchanges: These include platforms such as Coinbase and Binance. They're built specifically for crypto, so they usually offer the widest selection of coins and the most advanced crypto-focused tools. That can be a plus if you want flexibility, but it also offers more chances to chase obscure altcoins or trade more than you can afford.

Payment apps: Apps such as Cash App and PayPal let users buy crypto in a more familiar, stripped-down interface. These can be appealing if you already use the app and want a quick way to enter the market. The trade-off is usually higher fees on small purchases and fewer coins to choose from. If you're only working with $100, staying mindful of fees is crucial.

Brokers and trading apps: Some mainstream investing platforms — such as Robinhood, Interactive Brokers, and Public — also offer crypto trading. These can be convenient if you already invest there and want to keep your financial life under one roof. But it's still important to compare fees, spreads, and available coins.

Most platforms let you buy fractional amounts, so your $100 can still get invested without having to purchase a whole coin.

If you're buying crypto for the first time, simplicity matters. A flashy app with endless charts, coin recommendations, or gamification features like exploding confetti when you place a trade may feel exciting, but it can push beginners into trading too often. A boring, easy-to-use platform is usually the best move.

Step 3: Pick the best crypto to buy with $100

There are thousands of cryptocurrencies on the market, and truthfully, most of them probably aren't worth your attention. Crypto is crowded with meme coins, low-quality projects, and thinly veiled pump-and-dump schemes.

If you're only starting with $100, there's a strong case for sticking with established cryptocurrencies, such as bitcoin or ether .

Bitcoin and ethereum are still volatile, but they've been around longer, have broader adoption, and offer more liquidity than you'll see in newer or more speculative tokens.

"At this point, over-diversifying into many different coins doesn't often lead to better returns — but it does add more risk," said Blumberg.

Step 4: Set up your account, deposit funds, and make your first trade

Next, it's time to set up your account. This usually involves entering personal information, verifying your identity, and linking a bank account or debit card.

Once your account is set up, you can deposit your funds and place your first trade. Review the purchase amount, check the fees, and make sure you understand what you're buying before you hit confirm.

If you think you may want to keep investing over time, you might also consider setting up recurring purchases. This helps you practice dollar-cost averaging, which means investing a set amount at regular intervals instead of putting all your money in at once. This can help you build a position gradually and smooth out your purchase price over time instead of trying to anticipate the perfect entry point.

You won't owe taxes for buying and holding crypto. But selling crypto for a profit — or exchanging one coin for another coin — is a capital gain and considered a taxable event in the eyes of the IRS.

If you sell crypto in 2026 through a U.S. exchange or broker, that platform now must send you and the IRS a Form 1099-DA showing key details from the sale, such as the transaction date, proceeds, and, in some cases, cost basis information.

That moves crypto closer to the same kind of tax reporting investors already know from Form 1099-B for stocks and mutual funds.

In the past, most crypto investors received little or no standardized tax reporting from exchanges, which made it easier to underreport gains, "forget" trades, or assume the IRS wouldn't connect the dots.

With Form 1099-DA — which rolled out to consumers for the first time in calendar year 2026 — there are fewer gray areas and a much clearer paper trail. So if you're selling crypto, it's more important than ever to treat taxation here as seriously as you would with stocks or other investments.

If your goal is long-term crypto exposure and you want to avoid taxable trades, one alternative is buying crypto-related exchange-traded funds in a tax-advantaged account, such as an IRA . In a traditional IRA, taxes are generally deferred until you withdraw the money, while qualified Roth IRA withdrawals can be tax-free.

There are currently only three types of cryptocurrency ETFs on the market — bitcoin, ether, and solano — but buying and selling them inside an IRA won't trigger capital gains tax the way it would inside a regular taxable account.

Step 6: Monitor your trade — but not too closely

After getting your money in the market, the next step is mostly patience. Crypto prices can swing sharply in a single day, so don't be surprised if your $100 rises or falls quickly.

"Be prepared to wake up in the morning to market moves, without always a clear understanding as to the reason," said Blumberg.

That's why position sizing matters. Starting with $100 is smart because it limits the damage if things go badly or if you decide crypto isn't for you. If you end up liking the asset class and want more exposure later, you can always add gradually.

It's also smart to monitor your own behavior. If you're checking prices constantly, chasing hype online, or feeling tempted to buy and sell based on emotion, that's a problem. The goal is to stay informed without becoming reactive.

"Investors should have their expectation and thesis in mind as they watch the movements in price," said Blumberg.

Let the trade teach you something, build your confidence, and then decide what comes next.

articles.title: Coinbase Stock Surges On Plans To Offer Retail Investors Early IPO Access
articles.summary: The price of Bitcoin also rose on Monday, and was up over $85,000.
articles.body:
Coinbase's stock price jumped 4.5% on Monday, hours after the company announced plans to allow retail investors early access to initial public offerings—and after bitcoin's rally pushed it over $85,000.

Shares of COIN were up about 4.4% around 12:30 p.m. EDT on Monday, trading at $202.74 per share.

Bitcoin reached $85,000 by midday, extending a rally even after the Senate failed to pass the CLARITY Act, the landmark crypto legislation setting up a regulatory framework for the industry.

The jump happened hours after Coinbase announced it would begin offering customers the opportunity to access IPO shares before companies open on the market by allowing them to submit a "conditional offer to buy" after a company's price range is made public.

Coinbase will then distribute shares to investors, but the company warned these orders could be "filled in full, in part, or not at all" based on supply from underwriters and demand from customers.

The company also said these shares would be allotted by an algorithm with "established methodology" that prioritizes long-term investors, and users that get banned for selling IPO shares too early could see fewer allotments using this system.

Oura's upcoming IPO will be the first Coinbase customers will be able to access early, according to a blog post on Monday. Oura, a wellness tech company that sells smart rings that collect health data, is planning to go public soon, and in an amended Securities and Exchange Commission filing on Monday said it planned to sell 50 million shares at prices between $40-$44, looking to raise up to $2.2 billion.

Coinbase's surge on Monday comes days after the company filed paperwork to start selling "perpetual futures," or speculative derivative contracts that don't expire, pegged to several major U.S. stocks. In a post on X on Friday, Coinbase said it was planning to "bring liquid, 24/5 exposure to individual stocks in the US for the first time." The Commodities Futures Exchange Commission only approved this type of contract in May. Coinbase plans to start offering these contracts on 50 to 60 major stocks, including Apple, Tesla and Nvidia, later this year, the Wall Street Journal reported.

articles.title: Retired senior citizen teacher deposited Rs 1.33 crore cash, but filed no ITR; taxman added Rs 48.73 lakh, ITAT quashes reassessment, here’s why
articles.summary: India Business News: A retired school teacher from Mysore, Karnataka, found himself facing income tax reassessment proceedings after cash deposits totalling Rs 1.33 crore .
articles.body: A retired school teacher from Mysore, Karnataka, found himself facing income tax reassessment proceedings after cash deposits totalling Rs 1.33 crore in his bank accounts were flagged under the Central Board of Direct Taxes' (CBDT) risk management strategy (RMS).The Income Tax Department also noted that the individuals had not filed an income tax return (ITR) for the relevant year. This meant the department did not have details of the income he had earned during the period under scrutiny.The department was aware that agriculture and interest from savings bank accounts were his stated primary sources of income. What it did not have, however, was information about the actual income he had earned from either source.What the case is aboutThe cash deposits consequently prompted the department to examine whether the senior citizen had any income that had not been disclosed for assessment year (AY) 2015-16. It began the reassessment process by sending him a tax notice.The transactions identified through the CBDT's RMS for AY 2015-16 were:A cash deposit of Rs 13 lakh in a savings bank account. This fell within the category of cash deposits of Rs 10 lakh or more.A cash deposit of Rs 60 lakh, which was also reported under the category of cash deposits of Rs 10 lakh or more in a savings bank account.Cash deposits of Rs 50,000 and aboveBank interest: Rs 12,701 recorded under "Interest other than Interest on Securities", Section 194A.It’s important to note that the first notice was issued to the senior citizen under Section 148A(b) on March 26, 2022. He did not respond to it.The next step came on April 26, 2022, when the Assessing Officer (AO) passed the order under Section 148A(d), determining that the case was fit for reopening the assessment for AY 2015-16 under Section 148,according to an ET report.A Section 148 notice was issued the same day, requiring the individual to file his ITR for AY 2015-16 within 30 days from the date on which he received the notice.This time the senior citizen did file an ITR in response to the notice. However, the income tax return was not e-verified and was therefore treated as invalid.The AO subsequently issued notices under Section 142(1) and show-cause notices on. The individual on his part complied with these notices only to a limited extent.The reassessment proceedings ultimately resulted in an order which was passed by the AO under Section 147 read with Section 144 on February 29, 2024. The senior citizen’s total assessed income was determined at Rs 48.85 lakh.The tax filer then challenged the assessment before the CIT (A), but the appeal was dismissed following the hearing. He then took the matter to the ITAT Bangalore.What ITAT Bangalore ruled and why the person won the caseThe SMC Bench of the ITAT heard the senior citizen’s appeal on April 15, 2026, and subsequently passed its order in his favour on July 10, 2026.The issue that proved decisive was not the amount of cash deposited, but the timing of the reassessment notice.For AY 2015-16, March 31, 2022 was the last date for issuing the reassessment notice. However, the Section 148 notice in this case was issued on April 26, 2022, 26 days after the limitation period had ended.The ITAT Bangalore took note of this delay and held that the notice had been issued after the prescribed period had already expired.Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET that the ITAT Bangalore decided the matter on the question of jurisdiction arising from the limitation period. Once the tribunal found that the Section 148 notice had been issued beyond the prescribed period and was therefore invalid, the reassessment proceedings based on that notice could not continue.The tribunal considered decisions of earlier coordinate benches while examining the issue. It also relied on the principles laid down by the Supreme Court in the Rajeev Bansal case and by the Karnataka High Court in Mohammed Yaseen. These decisions clarified that, for AY 2015-16, reassessment notices issued after the expiry of the earlier six-year limitation period could not be sustained.The ITAT therefore quashed the Section 148 notice and the reassessment order passed under Section 147, and allowed the assessee's appeal.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Moneyview targets Rs 5,985 cr IPO valuation, 20% below 2022 round
articles.summary: India Business News: Moneyview sets Rs 32-34 IPO price band, targeting Rs 5,985 crore valuation—20% below 2022 round; issue opens Sept 24-28 to raise Rs 1,092 crore.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Digital lender Moneyview is set to enter the public market at a valuation lower than its last private funding round, reflecting a reset from the levels assigned to the company during the funding boom.The company’s price band of Rs 32-34 per share values it at about Rs 5,985 crore ($600 million) at the upper end. This is around 20% below the roughly Rs 7,500-crore valuation at which Moneyview last raised primary capital in 2022.The IPO will open for subscription on Sept 24 and close on Sept 28. At the top of the price band, Moneyview plans to raise about Rs 1,092 crore. This comprises a fresh issue of Rs 750 crore and an offer for sale of up to 10 crore shares worth about Rs 342 crore.Moneyview raised $75 million in 2022 at a post-money valuation of $900 million. The round was led by Apis Partners and included Tiger Global, Winter Capital and Evolvence.The company has also reduced the size of its public offering from what it proposed earlier. Its fresh issue has been cut by half from Rs 1,500 crore, while the OFS has been reduced from 13.6 crore shares to about 10 crore shares.Of the fresh proceeds, Rs 325 crore will be used to support lending under default-loss guarantee arrangements. Another Rs 250 crore will strengthen the capital base of Moneyview’s non-banking finance subsidiary, Whizdm Finance.Moneyview’s operating revenue rose 50% year-on-year to Rs 1,041 crore in the June quarter, while net profit increased 74% to Rs 67 crore. For 2025-26, revenue grew 43% to Rs 3,351 crore and net profit stood at Rs 243 crore, compared with Rs 240 crore a year earlier.Founded in 2014, Moneyview offers loans, insurance, credit cards, digital gold and payment services through its platform and financial partners.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Meta stock rockets 10% on price target increase, Muse AI downloads
articles.summary: Meta stock climbs 10%.
articles.body:
Meta ( META ) stock rose more than 10% in intraday trading after Wells Fargo raised its price target on the company and its Meta Muse AI agent app hit the top spot on Apple's ( AAPL ) App Store.

In a note to investors, Ken Gawrelski raised his price target on the company from $640 to $796.

Gawrelski pointed to Meta's recent successful AI model launches, including its latest Muse Spark offering and the Muse assistant, as proof that the company "now has a story to tell" with regard to its AI capabilities and services.

Meta's AI fortunes mark a sharp turnaround from last year, when the company was dealing with AI model delays and questions about the billions it is spending on its AI infrastructure build-out.

Since then, CEO Mark Zuckerberg has rebuilt Meta's AI lab, hiring Scale.AI co-founder and CEO Alexandr Wang as Meta's chief AI officer.

The company now offers several models within its Muse AI family.

The price target change and strong showing from Muse come ahead of Meta's upcoming Meta Connect conference on Wednesday.

Zuckerberg is scheduled to deliver a keynote outlining the company's upcoming plans across both its AI and wearables devices.

Meta stock has struggled over the past 12 months, falling roughly 5% versus Amazon ( AMZN ) stock, which is up 38%, and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) stock, which rose 11%. Microsoft ( MSFT ) has barely outpaced Meta, which is down 4%.

But Meta stock has jumped significantly over the past three months, soaring 30%. Only Microsoft outpaced Meta, rocketing 35%.
